transcript.speaker: Agent
transcript.text: Good morning, thank you for calling S-Net mobile support. My name is Toby. How can I help you today?

transcript.speaker: Customer
transcript.text: Hi Toby, my name is Thaddeus. I just got a text message saying I have used 100 percent of my 50 gigabyte monthly data allowance, and my mobile data has been cut off!

transcript.speaker: Agent
transcript.text: I am so sorry for the shock of having your mobile data cut off like that, and I completely understand how stressful it is to see your entire allowance gone.

transcript.speaker: Customer
transcript.text: What makes no sense at all is that my monthly billing cycle only reset four days ago on the fourteenth of October! How on earth could 50 gigabytes vanish in four days?

transcript.speaker: Agent
transcript.text: I can certainly appreciate why you are baffled and frustrated seeing four weeks of data disappear in just four days. Let's get your mobile account verified and investigate the usage logs.

transcript.speaker: Customer
transcript.text: Yes please, I'm travelling on the train to Manchester for client meetings today and I can't even open my maps or tether my tablet.

transcript.speaker: Agent
transcript.text: I will do everything I can to get you back online for your trip today. Could you please confirm the first line of your billing address and your four-digit security PIN?

transcript.speaker: Customer
transcript.text: Sure, the first line of my address is 41 Caledonia Terrace, Edinburgh, and my four-digit security PIN is 9074.

transcript.speaker: Agent
transcript.text: Thank you, that is all verified on my screen. So just to confirm, your account number is 8841209, you are on the S-Net Unlimited Calls 50GB SIM plan, and your cycle resets on the fourteenth, is that right?

transcript.speaker: Customer
transcript.text: Yes, account 8841209 and the cycle resets on the fourteenth. And I bought my new iPhone 15 Pro last week, which is what I have the S-Net SIM card in right now.

transcript.speaker: Agent
transcript.text: Right, I have the live radius session audit tool open here. Let me ask you a few probing questions about what you have been doing on the handset over the last four days.

transcript.speaker: Customer
transcript.text: Honestly, just normal emails, WhatsApp messages, and checking train times! I haven't watched Netflix or downloaded any games on mobile data.

transcript.speaker: Agent
transcript.text: Did you transfer a large library of photos or record any high-resolution 4K videos over the weekend after setting up your new handset?

transcript.speaker: Customer
transcript.text: Well, yes, when I set the phone up on Friday I restored my camera roll from my old handset, and then on Saturday I filmed my daughter's orchestra concert in 4K.

transcript.speaker: Agent
transcript.text: And when you were filming that orchestra concert on Saturday and travelling home on Sunday, was the handset connected to Wi-Fi or out on the 5G mobile network?

transcript.speaker: Customer
transcript.text: The concert hall had no Wi-Fi, so I was on 5G all Saturday afternoon, and even at home our broadband router upstairs is a bit patchy in the living room.

transcript.speaker: Agent
transcript.text: Have you also had your Personal Hotspot switched on over the weekend for your tablet or laptop, or was all the usage directly on the handset itself?

transcript.speaker: Customer
transcript.text: No, I haven't turned Personal Hotspot on since last month—I only tried to turn it on twenty minutes ago on the train when I got the text saying my data was barred.

transcript.speaker: Agent
transcript.text: That is a huge clue. Please bear with me for a moment while I pull the packet-data session breakdown from the fourteenth of October through to this morning.

transcript.speaker: Agent
transcript.text: Thank you for holding, I really appreciate your patience while the network radius logs loaded up on my terminal.

transcript.speaker: Customer
transcript.text: No worries at all, Toby. Could you see what ate all the data?

transcript.speaker: Agent
transcript.text: Yes, the session log is crystal clear. On the fourteenth and fifteenth of October, your SIM used less than four hundred megabytes per day on normal web browsing and email.

transcript.speaker: Customer
transcript.text: Right, four hundred megabytes a day is my normal usage!

transcript.speaker: Agent
transcript.text: Then between Saturday at four o'clock in the afternoon and Sunday evening, your SIM card transferred 46.8 gigabytes of encrypted upstream and downstream traffic to cloud storage servers.

transcript.speaker: Customer
transcript.text: 46.8 gigabytes in thirty hours?! From the orchestra concert videos and my camera roll?

transcript.speaker: Agent
transcript.text: Exactly right. One minute of 4K video at sixty frames per second is roughly four hundred megabytes, so an hour of 4K footage plus restoring your old photo library easily exceeds 45 gigabytes.

transcript.speaker: Customer
transcript.text: Wait, why would my phone upload and download 46.8 gigabytes of cloud photos over my S-Net 5G data instead of waiting until it had a strong Wi-Fi signal?

transcript.speaker: Agent
transcript.text: There are two settings on modern smartphones that allow cloud photo libraries to sync over 5G whenever Wi-Fi is unavailable or slightly weak.

transcript.speaker: Customer
transcript.text: I had no idea that was switched on! When you unbox a new phone and click through the cloud backup prompts, it doesn't warn you it'll burn 50 gigabytes in a weekend.

transcript.speaker: Agent
transcript.text: I completely understand how frustrating that is, and it catches so many customers out right after upgrading to a new handset with 5G speeds.

transcript.speaker: Customer
transcript.text: And why didn't I notice the 80 percent data warning text message on Sunday before it hit 100 percent this morning?

transcript.speaker: Agent
transcript.text: Looking at the SMS gateway log, the 80 percent threshold alert was sent at three-fifteen on Sunday morning while the overnight cloud sync was running at full 5G speed.

transcript.speaker: Customer
transcript.text: Oh, at three-fifteen in the morning I was fast asleep, and by the time I woke up it must have burned through the last 10 gigabytes as well!

transcript.speaker: Agent
transcript.text: Yes, the final 10 gigabytes finished transferring at six-forty on Sunday morning, and then when you boarded the train today the session refresh triggered the 100 percent cap lock.

transcript.speaker: Customer
transcript.text: Can we turn that cellular photo backup setting off right now so it never happens again?

transcript.speaker: Agent
transcript.text: Absolutely, I will walk you through disabling both settings step by step right now. Are you using an Android phone or an iPhone there?

transcript.speaker: Customer
transcript.text: I told you earlier it's an iPhone 15 Pro that I bought last week!

transcript.speaker: Agent
transcript.text: Oh, of course, my mistake—let's open the Settings app on your iPhone 15 Pro right now so we can lock down the cellular photo sync.

transcript.speaker: Customer
transcript.text: Okay, I've got the Settings app open on my screen.

transcript.speaker: Agent
transcript.text: First, scroll down and tap on Photos, then tap on Mobile Data near the middle of the Photos menu.

transcript.speaker: Customer
transcript.text: Okay, I'm in Photos and I've tapped Mobile Data... oh look! Both 'Mobile Data' and 'Unlimited Updates' are toggled green!

transcript.speaker: Agent
transcript.text: There is the culprit! Having both 'Mobile Data' and 'Unlimited Updates' toggled green tells iCloud Photos to upload and download full-resolution 4K video over 5G with no cap.

transcript.speaker: Customer
transcript.text: I have just switched both of those toggles off so they are grey now. What was the second setting you mentioned when Wi-Fi is patchy at home?

transcript.speaker: Agent
transcript.text: Tap the back arrow to return to the main Settings screen, tap Mobile Service near the top, and scroll all the way down past your list of apps to the very bottom.

transcript.speaker: Customer
transcript.text: Scrolling down past all the apps... right at the bottom I see 'Wi-Fi Assist' and 'iCloud Drive', and both of those are switched on too! And look, Photos shows 46.9 GB under cellular usage!

transcript.speaker: Agent
transcript.text: That confirms it 100 percent on the handset side as well. Toggle off 'Wi-Fi Assist' right there at the bottom so your phone never secretly switches from home Wi-Fi to 5G.

transcript.speaker: Customer
transcript.text: I've switched off Wi-Fi Assist and iCloud Drive over mobile data as well. That explains the whole mystery, Toby, thank you for finding that.

transcript.speaker: Agent
transcript.text: You are very welcome. Now, let's solve the immediate problem that you are on the train to Manchester today with zero data left until the fourteenth of November.

transcript.speaker: Customer
transcript.text: Yes, how much is a data add-on going to cost me? Because I really need my maps and emails working before I reach Manchester Piccadilly.

transcript.speaker: Agent
transcript.text: Because this was caused by an accidental cloud backup on your new handset and you have been a loyal S-Net customer at 41 Caledonia Terrace, I am going to apply a complimentary 15 gigabyte goodwill data bolt-on for you right now.

transcript.speaker: Customer
transcript.text: Wait, free of charge? A complimentary 15 gigabyte bolt-on for the rest of the month?

transcript.speaker: Agent
transcript.text: Completely free of charge—I have waived the fifteen-pound bolt-on fee on account 8841209 and lifted the 100 percent data bar on your SIM card just now.

transcript.speaker: Customer
transcript.text: Toby, that is remarkably generous, thank you so much! Now that we've turned off iCloud Photos on cellular and Wi-Fi Assist, 15 gigabytes will easily last me until the fourteenth of November.

transcript.speaker: Agent
transcript.text: I have also enabled an early-warning SMS alert at 50 percent and 80 percent of this new 15 gigabyte bolt-on so you will get a text long before you ever run low.

transcript.speaker: Customer
transcript.text: Oh, having a 50 percent and 80 percent alert is much better than only finding out when it hits 100 percent.

transcript.speaker: Agent
transcript.text: To make sure the network bar has cleared cleanly on the cell tower, I am sending a remote PDP context refresh from my console to your SIM card right now.

transcript.speaker: Customer
transcript.text: Aha, the 5G icon at the top of my screen just flickered and came back on! Let me check Safari and the S-Net app while I have you on the line.

transcript.speaker: Agent
transcript.text: Take your time, let's verify that both your browser and your allowance dashboard are working live.

transcript.speaker: Customer
transcript.text: Safari just loaded the BBC News homepage instantly, and in the S-Net app my dashboard now shows 15.0 GB remaining on my Goodwill Data Bolt-On with £0.00 extra charge!

transcript.speaker: Agent
transcript.text: Fantastic! Let's also check if your maps app loads your route in Manchester now.

transcript.speaker: Customer
transcript.text: Opening Apple Maps now... yes, live walking directions from Manchester Piccadilly to Deansgate just loaded straight up.

transcript.speaker: Agent
transcript.text: Brilliant. And because we turned off Mobile Data and Unlimited Updates under Photos, your camera roll will now wait until you connect to hotel or home Wi-Fi before backing up.

transcript.speaker: Customer
transcript.text: What about when I tether my tablet on the train? Could my tablet try to do a cloud backup through my phone's Personal Hotspot?

transcript.speaker: Agent
transcript.text: That is a very smart question. If you turn on 'Low Data Mode' under the Wi-Fi settings on your tablet for your Personal Hotspot connection, it will automatically pause background backups.

transcript.speaker: Customer
transcript.text: Oh, that's a great tip! I'll toggle Low Data Mode on the tablet as soon as I connect it.

transcript.speaker: Agent
transcript.text: Also, you can scroll to the bottom of Mobile Service in Settings and tap Reset Statistics today so you can track usage cleanly against the 15 gigabyte bolt-on.

transcript.speaker: Customer
transcript.text: I just tapped Reset Statistics right now! That is such a weight off my mind before arriving in Manchester.

transcript.speaker: Agent
transcript.text: Just to confirm before we finish today, is your mobile data working again and are you happy that everything is resolved?

transcript.speaker: Customer
transcript.text: Yes, my mobile data is working perfectly again, the 15 gigabytes is showing in my app, and we've stopped the photo backup from draining it. Everything is resolved!

transcript.speaker: Agent
transcript.text: Wonderful! Do you have any other questions about your S-Net mobile plan or billing today?

transcript.speaker: Customer
transcript.text: No, you have answered everything and sorted it out completely.

transcript.speaker: Agent
transcript.text: Thank you for choosing S-Net, safe travels to Manchester today, and have a great rest of your week.

transcript.speaker: Customer
transcript.text: Thanks so much, Toby. Goodbye!

transcript.speaker: Agent
transcript.text: Goodbye, take care.

transcript.speaker: Customer
transcript.text: Bye now.

transcript.speaker: Agent
transcript.text: Thank you again for choosing S-Net. Goodbye.

transcript.speaker: Customer
transcript.text: Cheers, bye.

transcript.speaker: Agent
transcript.text: Have a great day.

transcript.speaker: Customer
transcript.text: You too, bye.

transcript.speaker: Agent
transcript.text: Thank you for choosing S-Net, goodbye.

transcript.speaker: Customer
transcript.text: Goodbye.
